minutes.headline: Committee delayed its FY24 budget vote to March 22 and postponed the primary school AC vote to next week.
minutes.summary: A remote Lunenburg School Committee meeting, held during storm power outages, presented the superintendent's FY24 recommended budget and moved the budget hearing and approval to March 22. It reviewed a scaled-back air conditioning plan for the primary school, a class of 2015 fund request, and a snack shack (concession stand) policy. Final-read concession stand and transportation policies were adopted, and two school trips were approved.

attendees.role: presenter on the primary AC project

public_comment.topic: Resident argued the SEL curriculum lacks evidence of academic benefit, cited MCAS and accountability data showing Lunenburg schools declining, and asked the committee to re-evaluate SEL.
Resident raised equity and accessibility concerns about the May 1 busing form deadline in the transportation policy and urged a softer deadline.
Thanked the chair for allowing his earlier comment and a member for added context.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the class balance is almost sixty-seven hundred dollars. The committee wants named custodians on a bank account before releasing the funds.

Health insurance was budgeted at a higher increase than the rate that ultimately came in, giving savings. Savings were also found in furniture budgets and a technology consultant replaces a network manager.
The recommended budget is a stated increase over FY23. It is local funds from taxes and Chapter 70.
figures_as_heard: 22 million eight hundred and eighty three thousand four hundred and forty two dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Chapter 70 rose only slightly and the state funds a share of the local budget, the remainder from the town.
The budget includes a humanities teacher and an enrollment secretary split between local budget and the special education grant.
ESSER-, title- and special education grant-funded positions and tutors support MTSS, with no local funding to MTSS.
The reserve is described as appropriately funded, with custodial and cafeteria contracts unsettled. Circuit breaker and entitlement grants are still awaited.
The state increase is small, the town is giving the schools an increase, and the schools expect to receive all of it this year.
Town meeting appropriated money for AC. Engineers' estimate for a full fix was far higher, so split systems are proposed instead.
figures_as_heard: two hundred and thirty eight thousand

budget_items.what_was_said: Covering the remaining classrooms and two offices would cost additional money not funded now.
A member said the AC work came in far cheaper than the full estimate and the town should not expect that again for Turkey Hill.
figures_as_heard: six and a half million dollar problem

budget_items.what_was_said: The policy assesses a fee for items left behind.
The snack shack coordinator gave the cost of manager certification versus handler certification.
A member said free cash was reserved for the overlay account and the capital set-aside was reduced. A further amount might go to the capital plan, possibly funding the Turkey Hill fire alarm.
The school budget covers uniforms, jerseys and helmets while boosters can cover extras.

decisions.decision: The budget public hearing will be held remotely on March 22 at 6:30, before the Finance Committee meeting.
Class of 2015 funds will not be released until names of account holders are supplied.
The primary school AC vote will wait until next week so the town manager's next steps can be confirmed.
Policy 3204 will go back to the policy committee to tighten the gifts and advertising language and align with policy 1301.
Staff will seek clarification from the Board of Health on whether a manager-level certification is required; the policy was adopted as read.
Future topics: the scoreboard advertisement, bullying, and an athletics report with the new athletic director.

what_happened.line: The School Committee delayed its vote on the FY24 school budget until March 22, after the budget hearing, and moved the hearing to that date.
The hearing was moved to March 22 at 6:30, remotely, before the Finance Committee meeting.
The committee tabled the primary school air conditioning vote to the next meeting so the town manager's next steps can be confirmed.
Final-read concession stand and transportation policies were adopted; the transportation vote is not clear for one member in the captions.
The committee withheld Class of 2015 funds until account holders' names are supplied, and approved the Galapagos and Italy/Greece trips.

why_it_matters: The FY24 school budget, which is paid for by local taxes and Chapter 70 state aid, will not be voted until after a March 22 hearing, so that is the residents' chance to comment before approval.
The primary school air conditioning plan was scaled back to split systems, and some classrooms and offices are left unfunded, so more spending may be requested later.
